she is so sweet, good at explaining things, and fair exams. lab can be a little annoying but only towards the end. it is a useful and interesting class and i would take her if i could again

Dr. Frauwirth was an outstanding professor and I'm planning on taking his immunology class as well in the future. Don't get me wrong, this class is difficult and a lot of work, but he provides plenty of resources to set you up for success. The class structure was super organized, with pre-lecture quizzes each week, lectures with TopHat clicker questions, 3 midterms, a final, and the separate laboratory section. The lectures were engaging and Dr. Frauwirth has a great sense of humor. He also records the lectures which is super helpful for studying if you need to brush up on a topic. There are also a couple of extra credit points built into the course, which is nice. He provides sample questions for the exams and reuses questions from past exams which are also available. I found the exams to be kind of difficult, but I scored well on them. They included multiple choice and short answer questions, with 2 long answer essay questions except the final. This is definitely a material-dense course, but the content is actually super interesting and engaging, and it's cool to see how it aligns with other biology and chemistry courses. There is also a textbook, but personally I didn't really use it because his exams only cover content from the lectures. The laboratory section wasn't too bad, definitely try to get good lab partners. Overall I'd definitely recommend taking his class!
Good, funny, and knows his stuff
Literally the cutest professor ever. We saw him with his kids and it was so wholesome, we all love Frauwirth. His exams are really fair, he really knows his stuff, and he records lectures.

Anyone who doesn't love Frauwirth is an automatic red flag in my book, this man is the salt of the earth and truly a GEM. 
I wasn't supposed to have him originally, I had signed up for Parent due to all his sections being closed/not working for my schedule, but he ended up taking over for her due to some unforeseen events.
His exams are super fair, there's about one lecture quiz per week (pretty easy, open note), participation questions during lectures, and a couple in lecture discussion posts. 
The lab is also pretty straightforward, as long as you keep on top of your work and don't leave the lab notebook til the last minute (I did and let me tell you, DO IT THROUGHOUT THE SEMESTER) it's fine. There are two big presentations (both group work), one individual lab report, and one group lab report along with some post-lab quizzes, but all are fine if you have a good group to work with. 
All in all this class is an easy A as long as you put the time and effort into studying + keeping up with your work, Frauwirth is an EXCELLENT choice of a professor and one of the few I've had that I can wholeheartedly say is passionate, caring and patient towards his students.

He is overall very knowledgeable but can be extremely harsh. It was very humiliating to have questions about my exam and be made to feel unintelligent around so many other students. Nonetheless, he was always willing to help and provided many opportunities to do better.

Great professor! No crazy homework, TopHat questions in class. HOWEVER, THE TA MAKES YOUR EXAM GRADE. There was a significant issue my semester with one TA (mine) grading extremely tough for her sections compared to the other sections. Frauwirth did nothing to change this. This made the exams way harder than needed to be. Otherwise a decent class

I cannot recommend Dr. Frauwirth enough for this class. First of all, he is a very nice professor and it truly shows that he wants you to succeed in this class. The class was very organized, you will have an textbook quiz once a week due before the first lecture of the week, you will have questions during the lecture that are graded just for participation, 3 midterms, a final, and separate assignment for the lab. This class can be boring sometimes and it could feel a bit slow but Dr. Frauwirth throughly takes the time to explain all the concepts and everything going on and if you pay attention you will understand everything he is saying. There are a lot of free points that helps your grade. The exams are very fair, the multiple choice section can sometimes ask some very specific questions but the short answer and the essay portion of the exam is usually filled with broad questions where there are a lot of ways to answer and get all of the points. The lab portion of this class is very easy and for the most part you will get out of lab early and get almost perfect scores on all the assignments (depending on your TA). Overall, taking BSCI330 with Dr. Frauwirth was amazing and I learned everything while also not having to stress about my grade too much.
So so nice and thoughtful. Has a lot of points which help boost your grade and is always willing to answer questions! Favorite professor so far for sure

Biggest tip I can offer is: Do NOT slack on that final just because you've done well on all your other exams. The final is a real kicker! Exam content is very fair and the professor is very smart. Lectures can be very content-heavy and it'll definitely test your attention span, but you'll learn a lot!

Easily the worst professor I have ever had in my life. This guy is actually the devil. Exams were insanely hard and tested us on extremely specific and niche information that is barely talked about in lecture, not to mention that the whole entire test is free response. Our last test was 7 pages of free response questions that we were expected to finish in 50 minutes. The test averages are always in the 60's, and although sukharev is a nice guy, he is the worst at explaining concepts and often leaves students feeling more confused after his explanations. He does not assign readings or give any supplemental materials, and there are no TA's to give you guidance either. Would not wish this guy upon my worst enemy

Attendance CAN be mandatory due to top hats, but some have gotten away with just doing it away from class.

LECTURE-HEAVY. Get ready for content. He can be a little unorganized and blab away so try to keep an eye on what specifically he wants you to know for the exam. Hint** there's a ton of useful quizlets. 
 
Lab is tedious, it's a big waste of time BUT can be a tad fun as well as a great grade boost.

Very monotone voice that can be difficult to engage with at times. A lot of the class is review from other biology classes but ends up going more in depth. Lecture slides are packed with information so I recommend going back to watch the recording to make sure that you catch everything as questions on exams can be based on very specific things he mentions on lecture. The exams themselves aren't super difficult but it really depends on the TA you have (mine was a very tough grader with almost no partial credit). However, if you go to office hours he is likely to give a few points back.

Really great professor that makes lectures relatively easy to understand. I didn't find myself having to go back and review material super extensively after class. Not a lot of work, weekly textbook quizzes on canvas, lab assignments, and in class Tophat questions that are only graded for participation. Exams are relatively fair (some multiple choice questions can be pretty specific to certain lectures). Only downside is the grade is very dependent on the TA. My TA graded harsher than the others so many in my section struggled through the course. Frauwirth tried to be understanding but would only give a few points back on exams (if that) during office hours. Overall he's a good professor but I think the TAs need to be more consistent with their grading practices across the class.

I would not recommend this professor to anyone. He explains concepts very poorly, expects students to memorize far too much information, and does not provide adequate resources to prepare students for classes.

Expect the lecture to start about 5 minutes late, and to run about 5 minutes over. He does not care about students' time. 

I know him to be a very nice individual, but being nice is not what makes a professor good. He really should not be teaching this course as this is at least his 3rd year teaching it and is still getting the same comments. He teaches it like he's teaching graduate students who have nothing else to do other than memorize everything he tells them ... or doesnt.

He is not that bad of a professor, just the way the class is structured is hard because it is very exam-heavy and has very little supplemental work other than the quizzes. As long as you do well on the exams and lab you will be fine. He is a good at explaining certain things but tends to overcomplicate them, but you can tell he is passionate about his work and what he teaches. Overall would take it again, I took it with other heavier courses and it was not that much extra work. The study guides are word for word on the exam.
Good professors just use the study guide to do well in the class. He is passionate about what he teaches but tends to overcomplicate things.

Truly a horrible professor. Basically 0 organization to his lectures, 0 opportunity to practice any of the random concepts that he expects students to master, 0 concern for any of his students. It's crazy that a person can care so little about his job. Exams do not test material that was covered on the lectures because he doesn't even remember what he taught. Do not take a class with him if you can help it.

Please take frauwirth, the material in this class is easily so much harder than the other sections. Along with the fact that his study guides are not transparent at all and the exams are 40-60 free response questions with no Multiple choice or matching. Final exam was 75 questions all free response with 15-20 questions of material he never taught, expected us to memorize the codon table without specifying.

DO NOT TAKE. Take ANY other professor for this class. This professor does not care if you do not understand content, and he expects you to already have the background knowledge on the subject. On top of that, he does not teach general cell biology topics, but incredibly specific topics that do not need to be taught in order to understand biology. He also includes topics from other classes including BCHM461/463, PHYS132, and CHEM231 even though they are not required before taking the class. His slides will not help you learn the material, they are just diagrams copied and pasted from the textbook with no explanations or supplementary text to help the student understand what they are looking at. I spent hours upon hours reviewing material for this class for exams because he expects you to remember very specific details from his 40-page slides in order to write the exam. His exams are also COMPLETELY free response. The professor also turns away students from office hours, claiming to be busy, without an announcement in advance that he would not be available. In general, this class was time-consuming and I did not learn anything valuable.

Would I take him again? NO. But is this class doable? Yes.

Dr. Sukharev is a super sweet, nerdy, passionate guy! If you go to his office hours and ask him targetted questions (after doing your own HW) he will answer and explain the concepts. 
What makes him hard is HOW MUCH CONTENT HE PUTS. He definitely expects us to know significantly more than Frawurth (this is after discussing our content with Frawurth's students in BSCI330). As another person said, his exams feature all free response (drawing and question answer [explain how this works.. etc]). This is hard because he asks us to recall super small details that we would not notice in lecture. Our class was lucky enough to convince him to record, so he started recording mid semester. OH did I mention there are essentially no words on the slides. Meaning, you really need to either watch the videos or focus in lecture to understand what is going on. 

Alright, so you have to take Sukharev. What do you do?
- Mark any slides or topics he says will be on the exam. He is very honest with this. Make sure you understand the math inside out.
- He puts the location of the figures in the TB on the slides. If you do not understand a figure, look in the TB. If you still don't understand, ask chatGPT. And if you are still lost, go to his office. If you tell him what you know he will not be condescending towards you
- Practice drawing figures rapidly and concisely, he usually tells you what he wants you to be able to draw
- Understand the mechanisms well as he may ask the role of specific things in a mechanism or ask you to explain the mechanism and significance
- Go through the slides on your own and use the study guide as flashcard questions. I know the class will probably work on the study guide together (bec it is hella long), but if you do it on your own you will retain the info much better and it will not just be rote memorization. Feel free to reference the class version if you are lost, but try to do it on your own as much as possible and then seek help.

I know it seems like a lot of work, but it is worth it in the end. You'll come out knowing the material better than the rest AND you do not have to worry about failing ht final if you got super good grades on the midterms (yes, he does curve a good amount). You got this soldier. 💪

All the material you need to know for his exams comes from the class lectures. If he doesn't cover something in class, it won't be on an exam. His lectures are well-organized and easy to understand for the most part, but there is a lot of content, and they are quite monotonous. I fell asleep during multiple lectures, but catching up with the content was easy with the recordings. Sometimes he makes jokes though, which help make the lectures more engaging. Like other reviews have said, there isn't a lot of homework and the lab isn't difficult. I found lab fun, but it didn't really connect with lecture content too much. Make sure to keep up with your lab notebook; it makes it so much easier near the end of the semester. He also gives some extra credit with the TopHat questions and lecture quizzes, so make sure to do those. The first exam had less content than the rest, but only slightly. The exams are fair, but sometimes he words questions weirdly and his explanations if you ask him for clarification aren't clear. There was this one exam question that the whole class was confused about and his "explanation" of the question was frankly terrible. I probably would have gotten more points if he didn't explain. Exams consist of a few multiple choice, some short answer, and 2 long essay questions. The final is cumulative but only has multiple choice, fill-in-the-blank, and short answer questions. The exams and lab assignments are graded by your TA, so hope you get a good one. You can get a regrade for exam questions, but I've heard that Frauwirth is pretty strict with regrading.

Dude is nice and is generally a good lecturer. Exams are EXTREMELY lecture-heavy and contains a lot of specific content that he TALKS about, but does not put in the slides.

 DO NOT take tues-thurs 75 minute lectures. This man does not stop talking the entire way through, and I guarantee you will fall asleep, zone out, or generally pray for the sweet release of the void. The mon-wed-fri lectures are less overwhelming.

Consistently late to class. 

He once moved an exam two days before it was scheduled, then emailed everyone that he couldn't make it the day of the exam.

Unbelievably difficult to pay attention to, this man needs to take INAG110

He is the sweetest man ever. One short Canvas quiz per week, 3 midterm exams, 1 final. The lab is ridiculously easy so it will boost your grade if you struggle on exams. No surprises, concepts might seem tricky in class but are very study-able. Lectures are recorded too so you can go back and watch. Easy A!!!!

Literally the nicest professor I have ever had. The class itself is totally doable. The exams are fair, and he usually will emphasize the topics he wants to ask about on the exams so pay attention. He records all lectures so you can rewatch to study for exams. The lab is a super grade boost and there are is a ton of built in extra credit. Take his class!

You will hear that he was late consistently this semester, which is true, but it is largely due to him having a hard time with a lot of weird random stuff at home. 

You may have heard he is not a particularly exciting professor, which is also true. If you are seeking an exciting and deeply enriching lecture, he is not the professor for you. On the other hand, he provides a consistent and predictable (in terms of curriculum) course load that makes getting an A totally doable compared to other biology classes you will take, especially if you are a good student. Definitely recommend for any premed, this is not a hard class to succeed in if you have a little patience and a pretty normal amount of studiousness. There are small issues like boring lectures and inconsistent scheduling from the professor but for the most part you get what you put in with Dr. Frauwirth. Anyone with a crazy negative opinion is straight tweaking, dawg.

This is one of the most knowledgeable professors I've had at UMD. He knows how to explain difficult concepts in many different ways, and draws analogies to everyday life, so that anyone that pays enough attention can understand.

He does show up late to class. I don't understand why this would bother anyone, as it would only work in our favor as students. It means that we have less material to study, and shorter lecture recordings to review, since exams are essentially entirely based on what we cover in lecture.

He is also very nice and willing to talk with anybody to explain anything. He has a sense of humor.

He did move an exam forward two days, and then reschedule it to the original date. Again, I don't understand why this would bother anyone, because it only gave us more time to study. 

He also gave people that wanted to still take the exam that same day the opportunity to do so. So, if someone that wanted to take the exam that badly , and was that upset by the fact that we got more time to study, had a bit of patience and waited till he came to the class that day, then they still could've taken the exam.

Here's the deal: Frauwirth is absolutely the best BSCI330 lecturer you can get. His lectures are clear, engaging, and best of all, recorded after the fact. His exams are fair, and as a person, he's seems nice. You'll have to attend lectures because of the TopHat questions, but honestly, they are worth attending.

So, you're thinking, what's the catch? He's chronically late. To everything. We're talking ten minutes late to every lecture, rescheduling an exam twice, half an hour late to advising meetings, you name it. My friend and I have literally raced next to him the lecture hall on some days. I sympathize with the struggle to beat Beltway traffic, so I'm not docking a star for it, but if you're taking him at 9 AM, well, you've been warned.

Frauwirth is an okay professor. He knows his material very well and is very well-spoken. He also has lots of opportunities to gain more points with his TopHat questions and weekly quizzes. His exams are a bit hard but I would say just go through the lectures and know the concepts. Also, for the readings, please do not do them. They are a waste of God-given time. I was doing them the first week of school and they did absolutely nothing for me. He also has never smiled a day In his life. He is chronically upset all the time and a bit creepy if you ask me. Other than that, he's an okay guy. Also, he is always late. One time he arrived late to an exam that he pushed up and then canceled the exam by sending an announcement and moving it to the day that he had originally planned it for in the syllabus. What an interesting man.

Frauwirth is a decent professor. In lecture he will point out concepts he wants you to know and will stick to it. This makes knowing what to study very easy so anyone studious enough will do well in the class. In office hours he is very willing to explain concepts to people and often uses analogies to simplify complicated mechanisms. Due to these analogies however, it is sometimes unclear the depth in which students are expected to understand content, so study hard and you will do well. Also DO NOT RELY ON HIS PRACTICE QUESTIONS TO STUDY he posts them incredibly late :(.  He is constantly late to class, which isnt really an issue if you take him later in the day. the consistently late practice questions are why im giving 4/5.

Late to every lecture. His solution is to talk like he's auditioning for Gilmore Girls, and extend the lecture past the class time (cracking open a new slide deck with 45 seconds left), and yell at students who leave when the class is supposed to end.
Exams are intentionally tricky, feedback/explanations are nonexistent. not sure why others are being so lenient when he is so harsh to us.
to be fair, this class is pretty predictable and low effort when there aren't impending exams (that he moves around. multiple times. for some reason.)
He's very passionate about the topics but he's also a grump.

Nice guy, teaches thoroughly, and does keep to his promise of only testing what he covers in lecture. He does genuinely appear to be doing his best to make sure we learn. My only issues were these:
- his MC questions are rough, because they sometimes require hyper-specific knowledge of a single thing he said in lecture 
- he doesn't post practice exams in a timely manner (although this may be because of personal issues he has going on)
- doesn't respond to emails in a timely manner (you will likely need to talk to him in person)
- slides are weirdly organized, and do NOT contain a lot of the info that will be on the exam. He says this info in lecture, so be prepared for that. 
- isn't very clear when lecturing as to how what we're learning fits into a larger picture. But, to be fair, that's easily resolved if you spend time with the material.

Overall, biggest tips are to 
- keep track of which slides he does go over vs which he doesn't. Cross them out or something
- bother him in person if you need something
- try to review slides ahead of time so that you have a rough understanding of how the things on there work. Otherwise, sometimes you'll be completely lost during lecture (just because he does ramble and go out of order)

If you want to be able to do the bare minimum and get by, this is the professor for you.  There weren't a lot of assignments (in lecture) that required effort other than studying for exams.  However, he was very disorganized and tended to either over-explain concepts into the ground or breeze by them.  We were so behind this semester that at the end he just flew through as many lectures as possible, all of which he said would be fair game for the final.  It was also a bit confusing what to expect on exams because he seemed to emphasize the specifics in class, but there was always a couple of multiple choice questions that came out of nowhere.  
Overall, this class was easy in terms of getting the grades, but I would not recommend Dr. Frauwirth for actually learning the content to prepare for a career in research or medicine .

He was okay overall. I have a few peers who were very passionate about their dislike for the professor - mainly about his lateness - but honestly, I found that the class itself wasn't bad at all. The content is okay and the professor is fine, he's not the best but he definitely is not the worst. 

Cons: He nearly showed up to every single class late (though he did get better towards the end of the semester), and then would go over time. His lectures aren't extremely engaging, primarily because he sometimes went on a tangent over specific subjects and would reexplain the same thing over and over. Additionally, he would sometimes do the exact opposite and would go a little too quickly covering some topics. He also tends to be a bit of a slow grader and is slow to respond to makeups or emails (especially towards the end of the semester), though he always makes sure to respond at some point. 

Pros: Because he tends to be late and overexplains sometimes, he doesn't get through all the PowerPoint slides he has posted on Canvas by the end of the semester. That means there technically is "less" content on the final, since it is cumulative. He doesn't grade you on the content he didn't cover, so there is no need to study the PowerPoint he didn't lecture about. Additionally, he gives quite a bit of extra credit points, by adding additional tophat questions and adding an extra quiz. Also, I found that the content was not that difficult, especially since his questions on the exams were very straightforward. I also found the short answer and long essay questions fair. As long as you knew the material, you would do well on the exams, there were not that many confusing or tricky questions.

I have very mixed feelings about this professor. first of all the class its self requires little to no effort- there are weekly quizzes that are online and easy and then 3 midterms and then 1 CUMULATIVE final. the final is the kicker as at the end of the semester we were of course very behind so he just tried to get in as many slides as possible before the end. he is not very organized and my number one complaint Ould be that he would say what seems to be the most irrelevant thing in class once super quickly and never mention it again and that was fair game for the exam so your notes basically have to include every sentence he has ever uttered, the slides are not enough- of course using just the slides you will do fine but not great. also he records his lecture which is a huge plus since he does something go really fast and make no sense so at least you can go back and rewatch it. the annoying part is that since he records class you would think that class is optional...NOPE. he makes you come by assigning clicker questions which he gets really tight about if you do them without actually showing up. its annoying to have to go to class and watch him speed talk for 50 mins and then just anyways have to rewatch the lecture, all for 1 or 2 partition points per day. overall though class isn't terrible and the material itself isn't that hard its just alot and for some reason some times super specific memorization. 
the tests ar made up of multiple chpice- which is usually really hard and he is trying o trick you
short answers which are usually doable and then an essay which is also pretty chill. overall if you premed or this is a major option for you, there are worse classes than this for sure

Dr. Frauwirth is probably a nice guy outside of class, but I found his teaching style and his overall course design to be pretty bad. It feels like he's shouting at you throughout the entirety of his lectures and they are so incredibly boring. You also have to go to every single class (even though he posts recordings) because he is very strict about clicker questions. He's also a mess and never really tries to make students' lives easier-- he arrives late to everything, doesn't respond to emails quickly, double-books appointments, doesn't address points missed due to excused absences until finals week, doesn't give exam practice questions, does no curving/rounding, and refuses to give up even a minute of teaching time by always going past the end of lecture. His exams are probably the worst part-- they are so memorization-based and always focus on the nitty-gritty details from his slides or like 1 sentence he said during class. I feel like we're missing the big picture of what's actually important in cell biology when all we do is memorize enzymes involved in pathways and such while preparing for exams. He also has a very strict rubric for TAs to follow while grading and if you don't say an exact phrase you don't get points on a short-answer question. It feels like he's trying to trick you on every multiple choice question too. Overall, you'll learn cell biology with Frauwirth but it won't be a particularly enjoyable experience.

Pros:
- Lectures are recorded

- Lots of extra points. He has HW quizzes, lab assignments, TopHat clicker questions, and Cell Bio in Everyday Life (assignments where you have a discussion about how cell bio relates to everyday life and then write a reflection about what you talked about). Some of these assignments felt like busy-work, but the extra points from them brought my final grade up to an A even though I got a B+ on most of the exams. 

- Frauwirth makes it clear what you need to know for his exams. In the middle of a lecture he'll sometimes say "So if I were to ask you about this on an exam, you write..." When he says that, that's your cue to pay extra attention because you know that whatever he's talking about is gonna be important. That said, a lot of his exams just boil down to memorization of small details which was a little annoying at times.

Cons:
- Frauwirth's lectures aren't great. He will absolutely bombard you with information non-stop the entire time. It will test the limits of your ability to pay attention and stay focused, and you probably won't be able to keep up with how fast he goes. When I watched his recorded lectures, I found myself needing to pause every single minute just to wrap my head around what he was saying. 

- Your grade depends a lot on how nice your TA grades. I was lucky to get a TA who graded as leniently as possible, but other students in different sections weren't as lucky. Frauwirth didn't do anything to fix this because he seems to believe in harsh grading himself. I've heard him say that starting next semester he'll have the exams cycle through different TAs to reduce this issue, but don't quote me on that. 

- The readings for his HW quizzes are super long and are about material he hasn't taught yet. This made it way harder than it needed to be.
Hes a good lil guy. 10/10. class is super useful and absolutely worth taking.

he sucks. he grades more harshly than all the other TAs and when you go to ask him he acts stuck up and lacks any form of real empathy. he is always beyond condescending, has made multiple students cry. at the beginning of the semester I was defending him, but he truly doesn't care about his students at all. hell offer to help them before exams and then will disappear when they actually need help and reach out to him. if you are going to take 330 TAKE IT WITH ANYONE BUT HIM. his test averages were at least 6 to 7 points lower than the class average if not even lower.

He is the worst TA anyone could ever get. It is clear that he comes to lab unprepared, and does not understand the content himself. When asking him questions or trying to get help he become extremely rude and condescending instead of providing help. He often becomes aggressive and rude when asked a question he doesn't know the answer to. Outside of not being able to provide support to his students, his grading is horrendous. He often marks correct answers wrong, and grades questions incorrectly on top of being an extremely harsh grader.  Our sections averages were well below other sections, and often times students had to go to the professor to request regrades. If he is grading your exams check behind him and make sure your score adds up. 

AVOID HIM AT ALL COST!!!

Overall, I do not think this man should be allowed to be a TA. There is truly not a single compliment I can give this man as though I feel like he has done nothing that I have viewed in a positive light. Words cannot begin to describe how incredibly boring this class was, and I say that as a biology major. It was also kind of disorganized with him clearly using old slides at times or having technical issues and running out of time during lecture. He would almost always lecture a few minutes past the class time and to be polite you feel like you need to let him finish before getting up. He would spend lots of time in the beginning of class going over what to do for those who did not submit TopHat answers which was a bit annoying but also meant he'd have less time to go over class material. The class is basically a lot of repetition from other biology or prerequisite courses even though he said they worked on making this class less redundant. Lab was not really teaching you anything but also was not very rigorous in terms of the expectations.

Dr. Sukharev is a good professor, and there is certainly much worse than him out there. Few professors are as receptive to students' feedback as he is. If you put in the work you will do well. If you choose to be lazy, skip lecture, and use chatGPT to cut corners you will not do as well as the rest. This semester, I have found that the students I just described are the ones who complain about Dr. Sukharev. This class does teach you to hone your work ethic and prepare for exams well in advance. Furthermore, he is very well-versed in the content and knows what he is teaching. He is also generous with extra credit on the exams, but in a way that the students who listened to him and prepared accordingly will benefit from it. Enjoyed this class!

Genuinely a VERY GOOD teacher. Super knowledgeable and geeky. He goes over the essentials of what exactly you need to know for every exam, uses very neat concise slides with diagrams that aren't too confusing, and records his lectures. He also lets you make up any TopHat questions you missed as long as you let him know within a week of the missed day. The lectures are quick and boring (he Yaps with a capital Y), BUT the recordings make up for that since he explains the concepts incredibly well and in a way that doesn't seem entirely like jargon. My only complaint is that there is too much material assigned for one semester so it feels like he's rushing, our class had a handful of topics we never got to go over at the end but for the final he just drops whatever he doesn't get to. The guy spends way too much time going over TopHat answers
My tips for this class:
- Don't read the textbook, it's a waste of time (unless you really want to)
- He reuses lecture quiz questions and they can be easily found
- Use Anki flashcards for everything. Put the topics into groups of three, study one group for a couple of days then move onto the next
- Go over the recordings, skip through TopHat stuff and go back if you ever feel like you're starting to doze off. Seriously he will TELL you outright what you need to write down
- Ask ChatGPT to explain anything to you that needs more clarification
- Don't BS the labs. TAs do not care if you did an experiment or calculation wrong as long as you TRY. They know when you're just using ChatGPT to do your lab reports for you

The lectures are pretty straightforward and information heavy. You'll need to use flashcards, ChatGPT, and YouTube vids to help you digest and break down concepts better. The lectures are extremely boring and he talks a lot, but he records them on Panopto. He does tell you what you'll need to know for the exams (what questions he'll ask and what he expects you to know) so that's a plus. Your labs are totally dependent on your TA. Some TAs are chill, but my lab TA was too serious and everyone in my lab section complained about how he took off 0.2 points on your lab notebook for something. He says the textbook is mandatory but honestly you can just find a free copy online. I found the textbook useless IMO.
Some piece of advice:
- MAKE FLASHCARDS and review them everyday leading up to the exams
- Copy down the lecture quiz questions and the correct answers, make them into flashcards if you want
- Never study last minute. You'll have to start AT LEAST one week before the exam
- If you find the lectures boring, at least do something productive during that time and review the Panopto recordings later on 1.5x speed

All things considered, the class feels harder than it actually is. Your best bet when studying is to answer his study guides in depth, as soon as they are given to you, as they are fair representations of the types of questions he asks on exams. Many questions were word-for-word, and he was fair in not deviating from the study guides this semester. You'll lose your mind trying to memorize all the material and diagrams, so don't even try. Speak up for yourself, check your exam grades, because you can absolutely get points back. In my experience, most of the people who struggled exceedingly are simply underclassmen who haven't taken more difficult biology courses yet, or those who have a full schedule. This course requires effort, but on the bright side, the lab was kind of fun. Good luck.

Dr. Sukharev was actually a super good professor imo. His exams were pretty hard considering it is all free response, but it is all possible. I also felt like he at least tried where he could to make the lectures more engaging/fun. Thankfully he records everything so even if you are super confused or only have the mental capacity to listen for the day, you can always go back to watch again. This is especially helpful for the study guides when you need the answer verbatim. 

To succeed in this class you NEED to go to some office hours. I did not go to every office hour, but they did make all the difference when I did. He was flexible when I had conflicts with his scheduled office hours which was really nice too. He notices/pays attention to who actually goes in person to lecture and who comes to his office hours, and making somewhat of a relationship with him will only help you with this class. The exams will be 98% percent like the study guides that he puts out, so when you are confused by a part of the study guide, go see Sukharev because he will give you the exact answer that you need. Also go see him to go over your exams, because unfortunately when you get your exam back there isn't a key to go over. When you go to see him there are lots of chances to earn some points back, and definitely learn what the right answers are because you'll need them for the cumulative final. He really cares about helping students when they have questions. Definitely ask questions during the lecture because some content is just difficult and he will take the time to really explain it. 

Going to class and then using the panaptos for the study guides was the best way to do this class. Not all the content is directly on the slides and many times questions on the study guide will ask about things he had talked about and you will need to go back to listen to it. Using Knowt/Quizlet was my best friend. I would turn the study guide into flashcards and could put my own pictures on Knowt (aka directly from the slides) for my flashcards because you will be asked to draw a good amount of content on his exams (he actually prefers when people draw out their ideas). Then I would use whiteboards to write out my answers/drawings, use the learn modes. 

Keep up with the study guides as he posts them because if you wait til right before the exam it will take you awhile to thoroughly go through each study guide (they are divided up by ~3 lectures each) and you will not be well enough prepared. 

There are some built in curved-points on each exam, where there will be say 110 points scored out of 100. He did also curve at the end, but did not really say anything about it, so do not worry if you do a little worse on the final cuz the final is HARD. 

One note about the lab portion is if you can try to work with people you know are smart and capable because no one wants to be stuck in that lab for 3 hours and if you are with capable people you will always be done in 1-1.5 hrs. 

You def need to put some work into this class but i promise you will be able to get through it!!
Bad lectures; easy lab; no practice exams; difficult midterms; very difficult final; makes this class harder than orgo; avoid taking this class with Dr. Sukharev if you can

As a person, he's really sweet and most of the time just wants someone to talk to. He will also occasionally make references to his interests (Doctor Who, Star Trek, etc.). His teaching style is, unfortunately, a little disorganized. He tends to jump around a lot while he's talking and also goes into insane detail on some topics he finds interesting, but never tests you on them. However, his office hours are always open if you want to ask questions, and he's very nice if you approach him. Exam averages were in the mid/high B range, which is not bad for an upper-level bio class. The final was a bit harder though because he expects you to remember tiny details across everything he taught, so the average on the final was a C. He does use tophat to track attendance, but so many people don't show up that he can't track it anyway. He also tends to make jokes during class, and it's followed by painfully awkward silence, so if you take him in the future, please just give him a pity laugh or two T_T. How annoying the lab is depends entirely on your TA. My TA was incredibly petty and quite frankly, not that competent because I once asked him a question, and he used ChatGPT to answer it and gave me the wrong answer. Overall, the class isn't bad, and most people tend to do fine.

Not an organized lecturer at all. The only material he taught that I understood was the material that I had been exposed to in previous courses. The study guides weren't posted in a timely manor and I usually ran out of time to study. The exams were completely free response so there was no guessing for the most part. If you don't know the answer you are screwed. Hardest class I have ever taken. I enjoyed the lab and it was a good grade boost. Might have failed if it wasn't for the lab.

Lectures are jam-packed, but you don't need to memorize everything. You can study the day before the exam and still get an A. Make sure to listen to the recordings while working through his study guides—that was enough for me to feel prepared. There is also at least one or two biophysical problems on each exam that require a calculator, which should be free points. Personality-wise, Dr. Sukharev was very kind and understanding. He provided make-up exams for those who were unable to take them at the scheduled time. The lab portion is free points; no need to worry about that. Good luck.

Alex is the best. So helpful during lab and always has a smile on his face even during the 8:30AM section. Very kind and understanding person and definitely feels like I am supported in his lab. 5/5 goated TA.

Super good TA, clearly knows the content very well, and is great at explaining. Goes above and beyond to support us in the lab and is super approachable. Very kind and really wants everyone to succeed!!!

This class was very interesting. Prof. F does a really good job lecturing and keeping everything clean and captivating. He will explicitly tell you what will and will not be on the exams, and the general format of the class was very well put together. highly recommend.

Super interesting and engaging class! Professor Frauwirth is the GOAT, made expectations for exams and content very clear and class expectations/exams were fair. He's very approachable and is very helpful during office hours. He will sometimes jump into caveats about non-relevant material but overall I felt I solidified a lot of my previous bio knowledge and was able to learn a lot more about specific diseases and innovations that made the content more relevant.

Best prof ever, tries to make learning fun thru jokes. Only annoying part is clicker questions. He genuinely wants his students to succeed, and he doesn't change the exams from year to year. Get an old exam and you'll be fine. Will miss this class so much.

Dr. F is a really cool guy and is very passionate about what he's lecturing on. You can tell he really wants you to learn and that the class is very important to him. He has you use TopHat for participation (but it's 50 guaranteed points for going to lecture). The lab and the lecture are being separated next semester into BSCI331 and BSCI332, so I'm sorry for those of you that don't get the lab to count toward your grade. He does tell you what will and won't be on the exam, and sometimes he emphasizes not so secretly some questions that will appear on the exam. If you go to his office hours too, he will sometimes drop hints at what the essay questions will be. The exams are very fair, but you do have to study for them, but I never found myself panicking over the exams. I like reading the textbook just because that's the type of person I am, but it definitely prepares you for lecture. Only reason I'm giving a 4/5 is because he falls really behind on grading missed TopHat questions and slides aren't accessible through ELMS, only through TopHat.

I didn't have an interactions with Dr. Van der Weele, but she came into our lab once to evaluate the TA and she was really nice. The lab aligns really well with the lecture, and there isn't a ton of busy work. Everything was very consistent. I didn't like that no matter when your lab was, the lab report was due on Sunday night, but other than that, expectations and due dates were very clear. I loved my TA and the lab was actually interesting and filled with things that I may use again in the future.

D1 yapper. In the first 2 exams he had really good analogies, but by the time exams 3 & 4 came around, rewatching and taking notes on a 1 hour 15 minute video took 2-3 hours each. It becomes very confusing and tedious, and you will get tired of hearing his voice and nothing but his voice if you don't keep up to date with lecture notes. The Tophats were very fun, and the most engaging part of the class, but you do have to pay like 20 bucks for it. Never cracked open the textbook once, so don't bother buying. Fraurwirth isn't a bad teacher, but he doesn't like to give points back on an exam, and pray you have a chill TA. He is an absolute nerd, and it is very sweet to watch him relate things to Star Wars, or his kids. Yeah the exams are hard, so don't take the first 1 for granted, and he yaps A LOT.

GOAT prof - tells you what he's going to ask on the exam in class. Doesn't change exams from previous yrs for the most part - get old exams and you'll have an A easy easy easy. Only annoying part is you have to go to class bc of clicker questions.

He's an incredible professor and an even better human being. I loved coming to Cell Bio and I learned so much from taking this class. This was one of the best classes I've taken at UMD so far and Dr. Frauwirth is the best! Take this class with him - you will enjoy his class a lot.

Dr. Frauwirth is def one of my top 5 BSCI professor at umd. He is a kind and goofy guy but can really break down concepts concisely and accurately. He also gives a ton of extra credit around 17 points. The exams aren't too hard as long as you study for them you will be fine. The lab really depends on your TA if you have Shruthika Nallamaddi one of the best TA's at UMD lab will literally be a breeze if you have her. Overall fun class and not that difficult if you study for it.

As someone who was reading reviews for this class and super nervous because I was also taking a bunch of other content heavy classes at the same time, I am so happy to say I'm ending with an A! I actually did below average on the first exam, but I was able to do much better on all the other exams and in lab and that's what brought my grade up. Don't feel discouraged if you don't do great on the first exam! The class can be interesting and conceptually isn't too difficult to understand. It's just a lot of content that you need to know in depth. Dr. F's exams consist of multiple choice, short answer, and a long answer 18 point question at the end. My advice is to find as many practice materials as you can so you have some exposure to these types of specific questions. I would go to class and get exposure to the material, then rewatch lectures before exams, then do practice problems until I was getting them mostly right. Don't get discouraged! My only gripe with this class is how much content we are expected to know just a short time from being exposed to it and how specific and detailed the questions are when they weren't gone into that level of detail in lecture. I think this is unfair and as a result you have to put in hours and hours of work that I feel is unnecessary. Overall, Professor Frauwirth is a very funny and kind professor from what I've seen, and he makes classes enjoyable by making jokes and interesting analogies. I highly recommend you take BSCI330 with him.

Dr. Frauwirth is the best!! He is so approachable especially during his office hours, and he will always answer your questions in person or through email. His exams can sometimes be challenging on the multiple choice section, but the free response are very fair as long as you pay attention and study. He will literally tell us during class "When I ask you on the exam... you should say this..." He is very transparent about what to know for the exam and what to skip. In office hours he once said " I don't want you to memorize every single thing and lists of things that you can look up on google, but I want you to understand the main ideas and their importance." Lab is very dependent on your TA, but everyone typically does really well as long as you show up and put in effort on the assignments. Your exams are also graded by the TA so that could affect how much partial credit you get for the written portions of the exam. Overall, this class was definitely my favorite class that I have taken as a biology major besides BSCI170. We learned the typical transcription/translation and other foundational units of biology that you cover in every past class, but it never felt like anything we were learning was a waste of time or useful small details of information that we would never need to know again. I would highly encourage taking this class. You will definitely get the grade that you deserve through this class. I think it's very doable to get an A coming from a student that is never within the top percent of their STEM classes.

The material in this class is genuinely interesting, and Dr. Frauwirth does an excellent job breaking down complex topics into clear, easy-to-understand explanations. His slides are very clean and include a lot of diagrams, which really help with visualization. I felt like this course was essentially a summary of BSCI 170 and selected topics from BSCI 222, with some additional new material mixed in. Dr. Frauwirth also records all lectures on Panopto, which is extremely helpful for rewatching content. To study for exams, I would find a premade Quizlet and split-screen it with the Panopto recordings. I went through each lecture, added any missing information to the flashcards, and then drilled them until everything was memorized. This approach was usually enough for me to perform well on the exams. Studying for the final exam requires a bit more effort since it covers material from the entire semester. I reviewed around 600 flashcards and went back through all of my exams from earlier in the semester. The exams themselves include multiple-choice, short-answer, and one long essay question. Relying heavily on flashcards helped me get a 98% in this class. Another major plus is that there are many opportunities to earn additional points, such as TopHat clicker questions, lecture quizzes, “Cell Biology in Everyday Life” activities, and lab points. The lab portion of the class largely depends on your TA. My TA was amazing and graded very generously, but in my experience, most TAs are fairly lenient. Since the lab is worth 200 points, this can significantly boost your overall grade. Dr. Frauwirth also offered around 15 points of extra credit during my semester, including making one quiz extra credit and assigning a diffusion activity. Another important thing to note is that you don’t need to read the textbook. Overall, I found this class to be a relatively easy A for an upper-level biology course.

The final is cumulative but only has multiple choice, fill-in-the-blank, and short answer questions.

Frauwirth is a really nice guy, but his lectures are extremely monotone, and if you get the 2pm lecture right after lunch you’ll fight to keep your eyes open. He does Tophat questions for attendance purposes in lecture. He grades pretty uniquely that he has a set denominator in which he divides your total score by in order to obtain your final grade. This essentially means that if you do all the tophat questions, all of the quizzes, and any other extra credit activities, you get like 15 or 20 points of raw extra credit cushion points, so your ELMS score is usually lower than your actual grade. For exams, try to find someone who’s taken the class before. That will save you. We ended up running very late behind schedule in our classes, and we didn’t get to the last 8 lecture slideshows. I think part of this is because he spends the first 10 minutes of every 50-minute lecture reiterating the same points he talked about all semester (emails for missed Tophat questions, talking about the fact that he doesn’t round up, etc).

The majority of the questions on the final exam were from the most recent unit. I honestly don’t know how you’d study for it except know every detail about the things presented from the 3rd exam to the final, and remember your basics of the other 3 units (like which type of mRNA does what, Km/Vmax, principles of regulation, etc). He loves to ask really detailed questions, unfortunately, but the lab grade cushions your exam scores. I heard they are separating the lecture from the lab next semester, so I’m sure he’s gonna have to curve the class after that change takes effect.

Really nice guy, but quite monotone. Very accommodating though. I ended with an A.

Was the best TA I've ever had in college. Helped with literally everything in BSCI330 and helped with any grading errors or question you had. Hopefully she's kept as a TA for next year when they split up the class.

easy class, im bioE so i don't have many advanced bsci heavy foundational or advanced courses. i think i lightly reviewed lecture slides a day or two before the exams (and attended in person lectures) and managed an A-. i think the course is very dependent on your TA, which is unfair because mine graded pretty harshly..so hope you get a good one (although i think lab is seperated from the lecture next sem). pay attention to what he says, anything he speaks is usually tested!

Wow, I'm honestly kinda surprised to see so many positive reviews for this class. I agree that Frauwirth is a nice guy, but as a bio major, this class was genuinely one of the most BORING classes I had to take at UMD. If you've taken past bio courses, a lot of stuff entailed familiar topics, sprinkled with details that were hard to appreciate. We hardly covered any slides during the long lecture, and I felt like the dude yapped with a capital Y for an hour and 15 minutes straight. At the end of the semester, we were missing around 7-8 lectures' worth of material, so we didn't even extract the full benefit of 330. Also, the topics were so random that, most of the time, they didn't really transition smoothly into the next topic. Don't get me wrong, Frauwirth seems to be pretty chill and cracks jokes now and then, but it was so hard to stay awake during lectures. TopHat was literally the only thing motivating me to show up fr. 
That all said, if you want the A and that's it, it shouldn't be difficult, GIVEN a lenient, easygoing TA. It really does make a huge difference. Some TAs, I heard, were really harsh and barely gave partial credit for even overall correct answers. I never rewatched lecture recordings, bought the textbook, or went to office hours, but just understanding everything on the slides and getting access to old exams was sufficient. Please don't waste your time with the readings. Seriously, work smarter, not harder lol. Do really try to get a hold of past questions because you can grasp what Frauwirth wants you to know well and what to expect. Even though I'm glad I did well, this class was disappointing because it felt like all I had to do was remember material and spit it back on the exam. Overall, Frauwirth is a pretty mid professor, in my opinion, but try to get it over with or enjoy the material through other means. Cell bio is gonna show up again, after all.
Exams were pretty easy; he's a nice guy. But he talks a lottttt and we did not get through a large majority of the lectures (which could be a positive for some since less content on the final).
Material is interesting to learn, and exams are not difficult to study for. Just watch the lecture recordings.

name: BSCI330
title: Cell Biology and Physiology
description: Prerequisite: Minimum grade of C- in CHEM131 and CHEM132. And minimum grade of C- in BSCI170 and BSCI171; or minimum grade of C- in BSCI105. Restriction: Must not have completed BSCI230. Credit only granted for: BSCI230 or BSCI330. Formerly: BSCI230. Biochemical and physiological mechanisms underlying cellular function. Properties of cells which make life possible and mechanisms by which cells provide energy, reproduce, and regulate and integrate with each other and their environment. (Sponsoring Dept: BIOL). Specialization Areas: PHNB, CEBG, MICB, ECEV, and GENB. Students must pay a $40.00 laboratory materials fee.
